findings.where: setscreen.py:609 and :651-656 (move_range / judge_move, the turn's "every other gated joint 0.10 rad"); RULES :183-184; STAGE2_75_PLAN.md A12
findings.problem: Not a coding error: setscreen applies A12 as committed. But the rule it applies blocks the quick turn on the evidence available today. A12 replaces the 0.10 rad gate with A11's 0.87 only for the thigh twist; every other joint of a turn keeps 0.10 rad, and the inside leg's hip roll is under it in the design's own prototypes of the V0 quick turn. Under A11's third outcome that means no reference for the set and rate, turn conditions "not run", to the owner. Nothing in the design, the rulings or the plan mentions the hip-roll margin of a turn on the non-look sets.
findings.evidence: Screen's own functions (look._clearance_gates + setscreen.move_range, kind turn) on the 14 Nov scratch prototypes: design/cache/75-M-H-10_V0_turn_left_proto.npz -> twist use 0.817 (twist_ok True), tightest_other left_hip_roll max 0.0856 rad, ok False; design/review_mech/75-M-H-10_V0_turn_right_f0.8_review.npz -> twist use 0.817, right_hip_roll min 0.0857 rad, ok False; every other clearance gate True (mid-swing 0.0561 H, tail 0.8151 H, 0 interference pairs). Stage 1's own turning transitions on 75-M-H-10 (my own reading of q against plant.usable_ranges): hip-roll margin 0.0997 / 0.0878 rad (enter 0.35 rad/s left / right), 0.0718 / 0.0566 (enter 0.50), 0.0726 / 0.0727 (exit 0.50), 0.1003 / 0.1005 (exit 0.35). End to end in a scratch set, Stage 1's enter_walk_0.50_right marked as a causal turn: "blocks the freeze: joint range margin under 0.1 rad (right_hip_roll min) 0.057" with twist use 0.848. The prototypes used half-stride ramps (0.387 s), not the registered 0.375 s, and carry no tau, so drives and contact were not read on them.
findings.fix: No change to setscreen.py and no constant changed. The lead decides before work package S builds the turns: either accept that a turn whose built reference has a hip-roll margin under 0.10 rad has no reference (A11, third outcome), or amend A12 before any set is frozen, labelled as an amendment with these numbers. Either way have moves.kinematic / pick_stride_factor record the tightest margin other than the twist for each f tried, so the outcome is known at the kinematic pass and is in set.json stride_rules.

findings.problem: A file that begins inside a swing is screened, and its mid-swing clearance is read on the cut swing (clearance._swing_report takes 0.25-0.75 of the run it sees). The docstring assumes "a swing that starts on the first frame is a whole swing" without checking it. Every move planned for a set starts at a lift-off or in a stand, so this is a missing guard, not a wrong number on a planned file.
findings.evidence: Scratch set, Stage 1's stop with its first 20 frames removed (swing_u[0] = 0.3125 for the left foot): not refused; mid_swing_min_frac_H 0.0264 against 0.05 for the whole file; verdict "blocks the freeze: clearance swing_clearance 0.026". The same file cut at its end (start[:350]) is refused as designed. In all 18 Stage 1 transitions swing_u[0] is 0.0 for a foot in swing on the first frame.
findings.fix: check_swing_window(name, swing, swing_u=None): when swing[0, j] is true and swing_u is given, raise Refused unless swing_u[0, j] <= 1e-9 ("the <side> foot is <u> of the way through a swing on the file's first frame"). Call it with arrs.get("swing_u") at :725, add the sentence to RULES["cyclic_swing"], and add the cut-at-the-start case to test_a_window_that_ends_inside_a_swing_is_refused.

With no single-support CoP reading the CoP rule is skipped; with no joint_range_margins from the clearance screen move_range gives ok None (straight) or True (turn) and judge_move adds nothing. A walk with the same missing reading blocks (look.price lists a gate that is not True). usable_differs_from_plant is recorded but never acted on, although the twist use and the 0.10 rad margins would then be read on two different ranges.

One table row per case in test_the_table_of_what_blocks_a_freeze.

findings.problem: The 1 Hz forward-acceleration peak of a move that begins or ends in a walk is often the filter's end value, not the move's. The reading is the one the brief asks for and is array-equal to readings._forward_acceleration, so it must stay; but the block gives no sign that the maximum sits on the file's edge, and SCREEN.md prints it as the move's number. No gate is affected at these sizes (largest 0.42 m/s^2 against 1.5).
findings.evidence: All 18 Stage 1 transitions of 75-M-H-10: the maximum lies within 0.25 s of an end in 12. enter_walk_0.50_left 0.168 m/s^2 at 6.806 s of 6.808 s (largest value at least 1 s from both ends: 0.101); fr05_to_brisk 0.349 at 0.000 s (interior 0.179); brisk_to_fr05 0.259 at 0.000 s (interior 0.173). The periodic nominal walk reads 0.053 in the look screen. start (0.383 at 2.556 s) and stop (0.419 at 2.464 s) peak in the interior; a second-difference reading filtered at the frame rate gives 0.38347 against the block's 0.38345 for start.
findings.fix: Keep com_forward_lp1hz_peak as it is (the gated, registered reading). Add com_forward_lp1hz_peak_interior (samples at least 1 s from each end; None for a file under 2 s) and com_forward_lp1hz_peak_at_end (bool: the peak lies within 1 s of an end), and print "(at the file's end)" beside the number in SCREEN.md's column.

findings.problem: The sustained ratio is the RMS over frames, as the design says and SCREEN.md states, not over time. On a move whose frames are not uniform in time the two differ, and that ratio decides a1_over and the leg block. Inside a quick turn the frames are 20-35 % shorter than the walk's (stride factor 0.65-0.80), a larger contrast than any Stage 1 file has.
findings.evidence: Stage 1's speed changes (frame spacing 5.5-7.1 ms): tail cont 0.4627 by frames against 0.4543 by time (brisk_to_nominal, +1.9 %), 0.4812 against 0.4747 (nominal_to_brisk, +1.4 %); hip pitch +0.5-0.7 %. On the uniform files (start, enter_walk_0.50_left) the two are equal. The near band is 0.02.
findings.fix: No change to the gate. Record the time-weighted value beside it, reported only: a block key drives_time_weighted {group: cont_ratio} with weights np.gradient(t) repeated as sizing._motor_space stacks the sides, so a ratio within 2 % of 1 can be read both ways.

findings.problem: A walk's block is tied only to the look-format twin: arrays.sha256 is look/<name>.npz's, and nothing in the block names refs/<name>.npz, the file the bar plays and the freeze manifest lists. The design's 4.3 item 5 ("arrays.sha256 the entry's") read literally against refs.json's sha256 would fail for every walk. The equality with the ladder's rung forces arrays.sha256 to be the look file's, so the builder's choice is the only consistent one, but work package S has to know it.
findings.evidence: Scratch set: the walk block's arrays = {file: look/nominal.npz, sha256: e2bf5274...} while refs.json's entry sha256 is that of refs/nominal.npz; _current compares only with the look entry's sha256. The gap is closed elsewhere only by sets verify item 4 (q, qd, qdd array_equal between the two files).
findings.fix: In _job, add to a walk's block a top-level reference = {file, sha256} from its refs.json entry (add "reference" to WALK_ADDED so ladder_differences leaves it out) and make _current require it to equal the entry's sha256. Tell work package S that item 5 compares a walk's arrays.sha256 with look_sha256 and reference.sha256 with sha256.

findings.problem: Two things in SCREEN.md mislead a reader deciding a freeze. (a) Items print with three decimals, so a margin just under the gate prints as the gate. (b) For a turn the column "tightest joint margin (rad; the gate is 0.10 rad)" shows the thigh twist's margin, which that gate does not read on a turn; the margin that is gated (range.tightest_other) appears only in the verdict when it fails.
findings.evidence: setscreen._item(dict(limit="joint range margin under 0.1 rad (left_hip_roll max)", value=0.0997)) -> "joint range margin under 0.1 rad (left_hip_roll max) 0.100"; 0.0997 rad is the margin of Stage 1's own enter_walk_0.35_left. Scratch SCREEN.md, turn_roll row: "0.0455 (left_hip_yaw max)" in that column while the verdict blocks on right_hip_roll min 0.0566.
findings.fix: _item and _text: print values with four decimals (the table's own precision for margins). For kind turn print range.tightest_other in that column, with the twist's margin in the thigh-twist column beside its use.

findings.problem: Three places where a walk's verdict or the appendage exemption departs from what a reader of A12 expects. (a) verdict.text and rung of a set's walk carry the look ladder's sentence ("keeps its feature and loses that speed rung (character first) unless the owner decides otherwise"; "loses v_fr05 on 75-M-H-10"), not A12's outcome (blocks the freeze, dropped from the ladder). (b) look.price's item "rolling-contact split did not solve" makes a rung over a limit in the look ladder's screen but is left out of blocks_freeze here; A12 does not list it, and it cannot occur on V0, F25F9 or F25F9cl (no rolling foot), but it can on the look sets. (c) A1_GROUPS is sizing.SINGLE_GROUPS, which adds neck_yaw and jaw to A12's "neck or tail"; no effect on 75-M-H-10.
findings.evidence: review_over.py: the committed over-limit rung (75-M-H-10 fr05 V6) through screen_walk -> blocks_freeze [knee speed 1.012] (correct), verdict.text "over knee speed 1.012: under the plan's rule, ... (character first) unless the owner decides otherwise". review_table.py: judge_walk with over = [rolling-contact split did not solve] -> blocks [], within_limits False. RULES constants print a1_groups ['neck', 'tail', 'neck_yaw', 'jaw'].
findings.fix: (a) verdict.text = _text(block["over"], blocks, a1, WALK); keep screen_rung's sentence as verdict.ladder_text and compare that key in ladder_differences. (b) Ask the lead before any look set is frozen whether a failed rolling-contact split blocks (the drive loads are then not read); until then name it in RULES' reported row. (c) Either restrict A1_GROUPS to ("neck", "tail") or say in RULES.a1_over that the expressive head's two drives are treated as the neck's.

verdict: No blocker and no defect that gives a wrong number on a planned reference: setscreen.py does what section 3.7, D15 and A12 ask, and the one finding rated major is a consequence of A12 itself that the lead should settle before the turns are built. Coverage: a walk's block is screen_rung's block plus range and the verdict, and a move's block carries drives for all eight groups (cont, 1.25 x peak, 1.15 x speed), passive neck and tail loads, the re-solved contact with the CoP rule (-10 mm, or +10 mm for a causal move), grip need at mu 0.9 and 0.54, sway, accelerations, the five clearance gates and the range block. Walk: the nominal walk I generated in scratch from sizing.NOMINAL hashes to the ladder's V0 rung (e2bf5274...) and its block equals the committed stage2/look/screen.json rung on every key but speed, variant, seconds and the added name, kind, range, verdict; the ladder's own V0 nominal and v0.4 files through screen_walk give the same result (no difference). Stage 1's refs/nominal.npz priced the move's way (envelope._ratios on the file's tau and omega) gives the rung's 24 drive ratios with a largest difference of 0.0, and the last stride of Stage 1's start agrees with the rung within 0.003 on every ratio. Moves: on Stage 1's start and enter_walk_0.50_left the block's drive ratios equal my own formulas (difference 0.0), the passive ratios equal mine, the re-solved contact reproduces the file's tau, CoP margins and friction exactly and the entries' two recorded numbers (45.0669 mm and 0.34180; 45.0356 mm and 0.31943), the mid-swing clearance (0.05 H) and the tightest joint margin agree with my readings from the foot origins and from q, and the 1 Hz reading is array-equal to readings._forward_acceleration. Table: 111 of 112 crafted rows over start, change, stop and turn gave the blocking A12 prescribes; the remaining row was my own probe's rounding (0.87 x 0.3 / 0.3 = 0.8700000000000001), not the code. End to end in a scratch set (1 walk, 7 moves, one spawned worker): a turn with the tail over gets a1_over and does not block, the same arrays as a change block, a file ending inside a swing is refused, screen.json holds no wall time, SCREEN.md regenerates byte for byte, and a second run changes no file. Bit-identity: git diff --stat on stage2/look is empty (working tree, and branch against the working branch), the four committed look files hash the same in the tree, at HEAD and on the working branch, the edited screen_rung regenerates the committed over-limit rung (75-M-H-10 fr05 V6) with no difference, sentence included, and tests/test_stage2_screen.py passes. The major item: A12's "every other joint 0.10 rad" blocks the design's own prototype V0 quick turns on the inside hip roll (0.0856 and 0.0857 rad, twist use 0.817), which would leave the set without a turn reference. The seven minor items are a missing guard for a file that begins inside a swing, gates that pass when their reading is missing, the 1 Hz reading's end effect (12 of 18 Stage 1 files), the frame-weighted sustained ratio, the walk block's tie to the Stage 1-format file, two SCREEN.md presentation points, and the walk verdict's text with two rule-coverage edges. Not done: tests/test_stage2_look.py and test_stage2_motion.py were not run; run was not exercised with two workers; the prototype turns carry no tau, so their drives and contact were not read. Wall time per block on the shared machine: walk about 9 s, move 16-22 s.
